GraphRAG
A general approach to Retrieval-Augmented Generation that leverages knowledge graphs. Zep's community detection approach builds upon techniques described in GraphRAG, and it's mentioned as a promising area for future research.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
A framework for Large Language Model (LLM)-based applications that leverages Information Retrieval (IR) techniques to supply necessary domain knowledge to LLMs, typically for static document retrieval.

Large Language Models (LLMs)
Advanced AI models, often transformer-based, whose capabilities are limited by context windows and pre-training knowledge, leading to the development of external memory layers like Zep.

Query-Focused Summarization (QFS)
A task that Microsoft's GraphRAG system aims to enhance by capturing local and global relationships within document collections to generate summaries relevant to a specific query.

Microsoft Research
A research division of Microsoft, serving as the primary affiliation for several authors of the GraphRAG paper.

Microsoft Strategic Missions and Technologies
A Microsoft division listed as an affiliation for authors contributing to the GraphRAG research.

Microsoft Office of the CTO
A Microsoft division providing affiliation for authors involved in the GraphRAG project.

Knowledge Graph
A structured representation of information, where nodes represent entities and edges represent relationships between them, used by GraphRAG as an index derived from source documents.

Vector RAG
A conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach that uses text embeddings to retrieve semantically similar records, effective for localized information but less so for global sensemaking.

Sensemaking Queries
Questions that demand a global understanding and reasoning over an entire dataset, rather than direct retrieval of isolated facts, which GraphRAG aims to address.

LLM-as-a-judge
An evaluation technique where one LLM generates questions and another LLM judges the quality of answers from different systems, particularly useful for tasks lacking ground-truth answers.

LangChain
An open-source library supporting various graph databases for RAG applications.

LlamaIndex
A framework used for implementing the KG-GraphRAG methods.

NebulaGraph
An open-source graph database that integrates with GraphRAG for knowledge graph management.

Neo4J
A popular graph database that offers ecosystem tools and extensions for implementing GraphRAG.

HotPotQA
A widely used multi-hop question answering dataset.

MultiHop-RAG
A QA dataset designed to evaluate retrieval and reasoning across multiple documents in RAG pipelines, categorized into Inference, Comparison, Temporal, and Null queries.

MT-Bench
A benchmark dataset utilized for evaluating the performance of large language models acting as judges in conversational AI settings.

Adaptive Benchmarking
A process for dynamically generating evaluation benchmarks tailored to specific domains or use cases, often using LLMs to ensure relevance and diversity.

Persona Generation
A technique employing LLMs to create realistic hypothetical user personas, which in turn inform the generation of corpus-specific sensemaking queries for system evaluation.

Podcast transcripts dataset
A real-world dataset comprising public transcripts from 'Behind the Tech with Kevin Scott' podcast, used in Experiment 1 to evaluate GraphRAG performance.

News articles dataset
A real-world benchmark dataset of news articles across various categories, used in Experiment 1 to evaluate GraphRAG performance.

Comprehensiveness (Criterion)
An evaluation metric assessing the extent to which an answer covers all relevant aspects and details of a question thoroughly and completely.

Diversity (Criterion)
An evaluation metric that measures the variety and richness of perspectives and insights provided in an answer to a question.

Empowerment (Criterion)
An evaluation metric assessing how well an answer helps a reader understand a topic and make informed judgments, emphasizing clarity, reasoning, and supporting sources.

Directness (Criterion)
A control evaluation metric that assesses how specifically and clearly an answer addresses a question, focusing on conciseness and lack of irrelevant information.

Factual Claim
A statement that explicitly presents verifiable facts, used as a fundamental unit for claim-based evaluation metrics like comprehensiveness and diversity.

Claimify
An LLM-based method designed to identify and decompose sentences from answers into simple, self-contained factual claims for quantitative analysis.

Agglomerative Clustering
A hierarchical clustering algorithm utilized to group similar factual claims for the purpose of measuring answer diversity.

ROUGE-L
A recall-oriented metric commonly used to assess the quality of text generated by models, based on the longest common subsequence.

Self-reflection (Prompt Engineering)
A prompt engineering technique where an LLM evaluates and refines its own generated output, used in knowledge graph extraction to improve entity detection quality.

Leiden Community Detection
A graph partitioning algorithm applied in GraphRAG to hierarchically divide the knowledge graph into communities of strongly connected nodes.

GPT-4
A specific large language model, mentioned as an example of LLMs.

Graspy library
A Python library focused on graph statistics, specifically used for implementing Leiden community detection in the GraphRAG project.

Map-Reduce Summarization
A multi-stage summarization process used in GraphRAG where partial answers from communities are generated in parallel (map) and then combined into a final global answer (reduce).

LIGHTRAG
A proposed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework that incorporates graph structures into text indexing and retrieval processes, employing a dual-level retrieval system to enhance comprehensive information retrieval and improve response times. It also features an incremental update algorithm.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems
Systems designed to enhance large language models (LLMs) by integrating external knowledge sources, enabling more accurate and contextually relevant responses tailored to user needs.

large language models (LLMs)
AI models capable of generating human-like text, often empowered by RAG to access external knowledge.

Graph structures
A data representation method used in LightRAG to effectively represent the interdependencies among different entities, fostering a nuanced understanding of relationships and enabling coherent, contextually rich responses.

Dual-level retrieval system
An innovative retrieval approach employed by LightRAG that accommodates diverse query types by performing both low-level retrieval (focused on specific entities) and high-level retrieval (encompassing broader topics).

Incremental update algorithm
An algorithm in LightRAG that ensures the timely and efficient integration of new data into the knowledge base without the need for full reconstruction, allowing the system to remain effective and responsive.

Zirui Guo
An author of the paper, affiliated with Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications and University of Hong Kong.

Lianghao Xia
One of the authors of the LIGHTRAG paper, affiliated with University of Hong Kong.

Yanhua Yu
One of the corresponding authors of the LIGHTRAG paper, affiliated with Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.

Tu Ao
One of the authors of the LIGHTRAG paper, affiliated with Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.

Chao Huang
One of the corresponding authors of the LIGHTRAG paper, affiliated with University of Hong Kong.

Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
A university where several authors of the PathRAG paper are affiliated, and which hosts the BUPT-GAMMA research group.

University of Hong Kong
A university where one of the authors (Zirui Guo) is affiliated.

flat data representations
A limitation identified in existing RAG systems where information is stored without explicit connections between entities, restricting the ability to understand intricate relationships.

contextual awareness
The ability of a system to maintain coherence across various entities and their interrelations, often lacking in existing RAG systems, leading to fragmented answers.

Chunking
A vital process in retrieval-augmented generation that involves breaking down a large external text corpus into smaller, more manageable segments to enhance the accuracy of information retrieval.

knowledge graph
A comprehensive graph structure created from extracted entities and relationships, used in LightRAG to highlight connections and insights across a collection of documents.

Entity and Relationship Extraction
A process in LightRAG that leverages LLMs to identify entities (nodes) and their relationships (edges) within text data, forming the basis of the knowledge graph.

LLM Profiling
A function in LightRAG that employs an LLM to generate text key-value pairs for each entity node and relation edge, enabling efficient retrieval and text generation.

Deduplication
A function in LightRAG that identifies and merges identical entities and relations from different text segments, reducing overhead and optimizing graph operations.

vector representations
Numerical embeddings of text or entities, integrated with graph structures in LightRAG to facilitate efficient retrieval of related entities and their relationships.

Retrieval Component
An essential element of the RAG framework responsible for fetching relevant documents or information from an external knowledge database based on the input query.

Generation Component
An essential element of the RAG framework that takes the retrieved information and generates coherent, contextually relevant responses by leveraging the capabilities of a language model.

Data Indexer
A functionality within the RAG retrieval module responsible for building a specific data structure based on the external database for efficient querying.

Data Retriever
A functionality within the RAG retrieval module that obtains relevant documents by comparing the query against the indexed data.

Query Keyword Extraction
The initial step in LightRAG's retrieval algorithm for a given query, involving the extraction of both local (specific details) and global (broad concepts) query keywords.

Keyword Matching
A process in LightRAG that utilizes an efficient vector database to match local query keywords with candidate entities and global query keywords with relations linked to global keys.

High-Order Relatedness
The enhancement of a query in LightRAG by gathering neighboring nodes within the local subgraphs of retrieved graph elements, providing a more comprehensive understanding.

UltraDomain benchmark
A benchmark dataset sourced from college textbooks across 18 distinct domains, used for evaluating RAG models, including datasets like Agriculture, Legal, History, CS, Biology, and Mix.

Agriculture dataset
A dataset from the UltraDomain benchmark focusing on the agricultural domain, covering practices such as beekeeping, crop cultivation, and farm management.

CS dataset
A dataset from the UltraDomain benchmark focusing on computer science, covering multiple subfields such as algorithms, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computer networks.

Legal dataset
A dataset from the UltraDomain benchmark focusing on the legal domain, covering aspects such as case law, legal regulations, and judicial procedures.

Mix dataset
A dataset from the UltraDomain benchmark containing a variety of literary classics, including essays, poetry, and biographies, covering multiple fields such as philosophy, history, and literature.

Naive RAG
A standard baseline RAG system that segments raw texts into chunks and stores them in a vector database, retrieving chunks based on the highest similarity to vectorized queries.

RQ-RAG
An RAG approach that leverages LLMs to decompose input queries into multiple sub-queries to enhance search accuracy through techniques such as rewriting, decomposition, and disambiguation.

HyDE
An improved RAG method that generates 'hypothetical' texts to retrieve relevant documents.

nano vector database
A specific vector database utilized in the LightRAG experiments for efficient vector data management and access.

GPT-4o-mini
A Large Language Model used uniformly for all LLM-related components across baseline methods and PathRAG, including answer generation and evaluation.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)
A class of neural networks designed to process graph-structured data, leveraged by some GraphRAG methods (e.g., GNN-RAG) for effective retrieval.

GraphGPT
A GraphRAG system that fine-tunes LLMs with node-level knowledge, learning node embeddings for integration.

LLaGA
An example system where Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are utilized as an initial processing layer for graph data, generating structure-aware tokens for LLMs.

GALM
An example system where LLMs process graph data enriched with textual information to produce node embeddings or labels, refining the training process for GNNs.

OFA
An example system where LLMs process graph data enriched with textual information to produce node embeddings or labels, refining the training process for GNNs.

Grenade
A system mentioned in the context of LLMs-Graphs Integration, focusing on developing LLM-based agents capable of engaging with graph information directly.

Congrat
A system mentioned in the context of LLMs-Graphs Integration, focusing on developing LLM-based agents capable of engaging with graph information directly.

RankRAG
A retrieval-augmented generation system unifying context ranking with LLMs, cited in related work.

CRuD-RAG
A comprehensive Chinese benchmark for retrieval-augmented generation of large language models, cited in related work.

RAG-Ex
A generic framework for explaining retrieval augmented generation, cited in related work.

MemoRAG
A system focused on next-generation RAG via memory-inspired knowledge discovery, cited in related work.

PathRAG
A novel graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) method proposed in the text that retrieves key relational paths from an indexing graph using flow-based pruning and converts these paths into textual form for prompting Large Language Models (LLMs), aiming to reduce redundant information and guide LLMs to generate more logical and coherent responses.

A university where two of the authors (Zidan Yang, Zhenghao Liu) are affiliated.

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
A method that empowers large language models to access external and private corpus, enabling factually consistent responses in specific domains.

Graph-based RAG
A specific approach within RAG that organizes textual information into an indexing graph to capture inherent dependencies and structured relationships, contrasting with flat-structured RAG methods.

Flow-based pruning
An algorithm designed in PathRAG with distance awareness to identify and extract key relational paths between retrieved nodes, aiming to reduce redundant information and provide low time complexity.

Path-based prompting
A strategy used in PathRAG where retrieved key relational paths are converted into textual form and sequentially concatenated into the prompt for LLMs, ordered by reliability scores to guide more logical and coherent responses.

LightRAG
A RAG system known for its simple and fast approach, particularly its high-level key search methodology, which Zep's community search approach parallels.

NaiveRAG
A baseline RAG method that divides documents into text chunks and retrieves based on vector similarity.

Text-based RAG
A category of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approaches where external databases primarily store data in textual form, often organizing text segments in a flat structure.

Sparse vector retrieval
A retrieval mechanism in text-based RAG that typically identifies the most representative words in each text segment by word frequency and retrieves relevant text for a specific query based on keyword matching.

Dense vector retrieval
A retrieval mechanism in text-based RAG that addresses issues like lexical mismatches by encoding both query terms and text into vector embeddings, then retrieving relevant content based on their semantic similarity.

Knowledge Graphs (KGs)
Data structures used to represent knowledge as a network of interconnected entities and their relationships. They are employed in Zep to enhance RAG architectures for LLM-agent memory.

KG-RAG
A GraphRAG model tailored for the biomedical domain, leveraging specialized datasets and designed to link symptoms, diseases, and treatments.

Community detection algorithms
Algorithms applied on graphs to identify groups of nodes that are more densely connected to each other than to the rest of the graph, used by GraphRAG to summarize information.

Ego-network information
Refers to the immediate neighbors and connections of a specific node in a graph, used by LightRAG as retrieval results to simplify the retrieval process and handle global-level tasks.

MiniRAG
A concurrent work that leverages path information to assist retrieval, focusing on questions answerable by specific node information and exploring paths between query-related and answer-related nodes like KG reasoning.

Indexing graph
A structured representation of a text database in graph-based RAG, where nodes represent distinct entities and edges represent relationships between entity pairs, serving as the knowledge source.

Resource allocation strategy
A conceptual framework from which PathRAG's flow-based pruning algorithm was inspired, used to extract key paths by propagating resources through the graph.

"Lost in the middle" issue
A known phenomenon where Large Language Models tend to underperform when crucial information is placed in the middle of a long context, influencing PathRAG's prompt ordering strategy to place most critical information at the ends.

Comprehensiveness
An evaluation criterion used in LLM-based multi-dimensional comparison, assessing how much detail an answer provides to cover all aspects of a question.

Diversity
An evaluation criterion used in LLM-based multi-dimensional comparison, assessing how varied and rich an answer is in providing different perspectives and insights.

Logicality
An evaluation dimension used to assess how logically an LLM's answer responds to all parts of a question.

Relevance
An evaluation dimension used to assess how relevant an LLM's answer is to the question, staying focused and addressing the intended topic or issue.

Coherence
An evaluation dimension used to assess how well an LLM's answer maintains internal logical connections between its parts, ensuring a smooth and consistent structure.

History dataset
A dataset from the UltraDomain benchmark focusing on the field of history, covering various periods, events, and figures throughout time.

Biology dataset
A dataset from the UltraDomain benchmark focusing on the field of biology, covering a wide range of topics such as plants, animals, and insects.

NodeRAG
The proposed graph-centric framework that introduces heterogeneous graph structures for seamless and holistic integration of graph-based methodologies into the RAG workflow.

graph-based RAG methods
Approaches that enrich the RAG process by building a knowledge graph index and leveraging the structural nature of graphs.

knowledge graph index
A structured representation of information where entities and their relationships are stored as a graph, used by graph-based RAG methods.

multi-hop benchmarks
Evaluation datasets used to test the performance of RAG methods on queries requiring reasoning across multiple pieces of information.

real-world knowledge domains
Areas of information that are constantly evolving, posing challenges for static LLMs.

external retrieval mechanism
A component that allows LLMs to retrieve information from outside their pre-trained knowledge base.

multi-hop reasoning
A type of complex query answering that requires combining information from multiple discrete sources or steps.

summary-level queries
Queries that require synthesizing information to provide a high-level summary rather than specific facts.

data structures
Organized ways of storing and managing data, whose insufficient utilization can impede RAG performance.

structural information
Information derived from the relationships and organization of data, as opposed to raw text content.

knowledge graphs (KGs)
Graphs that extract triples (subject-predicate-object) to represent structural information, often used in graph-based RAG.

triples
Fundamental units of information in knowledge graphs, consisting of a subject, predicate, and object.

entity-event homogeneous structure
A type of graph structure used by some RAG methods (e.g., GraphRAG) where entities and events are represented uniformly, potentially hindering integration of diverse information.

local retrieval
A retrieval approach focusing on information closely associated with a specific query or entity.

global retrieval
A retrieval approach that considers broader context or aggregated information, often from communities or summaries within a graph.

coarse-grained retrieval
A retrieval outcome where the retrieved information is broad and may include irrelevant details, lacking specificity.

Heterogeneous Graph
The core graph structure proposed by NodeRAG, featuring distinct node types (entities, relationships, text chunks, events, summaries) to enable fine-grained and holistic information representation.

graph algorithms
Computational procedures applied to graphs to solve problems, used in NodeRAG for identifying key nodes and enabling fine-grained retrieval.

Better Graph Structure for RAG
A key contribution of NodeRAG, emphasizing the importance of and introducing an improved graph structure to better support RAG.

Fine-grained and Explainable Retrieval
A key contribution of NodeRAG, enabled by the heterograph and graph algorithms, leading to more relevant retrieval with minimal context and enhanced interpretability.

Unified-Level Information Retrieval
A key contribution of NodeRAG, where decomposed document information and LLM-extracted insights are unified as nodes within the heterograph for cohesive information handling.

indexing time
A performance metric referring to the time taken to build the graph index from the source corpus.

query time
A performance metric referring to the time taken to retrieve information from the indexed graph in response to a query.

storage efficiency
A performance metric referring to how effectively data is stored, minimizing the required storage space for the graph index.

graph indexing
The first primary stage of the NodeRAG workflow, comprising graph decomposition, graph augmentation, and graph enrichment, to integrate various types of nodes and edges into the heterograph.

graph decomposition
A component of graph indexing in NodeRAG, where text chunks are decomposed into primary node types like semantic units, entities, and relationships.

graph augmentation
A component of graph indexing in NodeRAG, which enhances the foundational graph structure by adding high-level organization and contextual insights.

graph enrichment
A component of graph indexing in NodeRAG, which adds unique and additional details to the heterograph, such as original text insertion and HNSW semantic edges.

graph searching
The subsequent stage of the NodeRAG workflow, combining the structural advantages of the heterograph with graph algorithms to efficiently retrieve relevant information.

prompting instructions
Guidelines or specific text used to direct the behavior and output of large language models.

entity (N)
A type of node in NodeRAG's heterograph representing named entities (e.g., people, places, concepts). It is non-retrievable and acts solely as a critical linkage and entry point within the graph.

relationship (R)
A type of node in NodeRAG's heterograph representing connections between entities. It is retrievable and functions as a connector node and a secondary retrievable node.

semantic unit (S)
A type of node in NodeRAG's heterograph representing a local summary or an independent event unit paraphrased from text chunks. It is retrievable and serves as a core node for graph augmentation and improving search quality.

attribute (A)
A type of node in NodeRAG's heterograph representing attribute summaries of key entities, derived from relationships and semantic units around important entities. It is retrievable.

high-level elements (H)
A type of node in NodeRAG's heterograph representing insights summarizing graph communities, encapsulating core information or high-level ideas from a community. It is retrievable.

high-level overview (O)
A type of node in NodeRAG's heterograph representing titles or keywords summarizing high-level elements. It is non-retrievable and used for accurate search entry points.

text (T)
A type of node in NodeRAG's heterograph representing full-text chunks from the original source corpus. It is retrievable and contains rich detailed information.

retrievable nodes
Nodes in the heterograph (T, S, A, H, R) that contain rich informational content and can be directly retrieved as part of the answer.

non-retrievable nodes
Nodes in the heterograph (N, O) that primarily serve as linkage or entry points and do not directly contribute to the retrieved content.

text chunks
Smaller segments of text from the source corpus that are processed by LLMs in NodeRAG for graph decomposition.

context noise
Irrelevant or unassociated content within a text chunk that can degrade search quality.

node importance-based augmentation
A method within graph augmentation that prioritizes selecting structurally significant and functionally pivotal entities for generating attribute summaries.

community detection-based aggregation
A method within graph augmentation that applies community detection algorithms to segment the graph and extract high-level elements for each community.

K-core decomposition
A graph metric used in NodeRAG to identify nodes in densely connected subgraphs that are critical to graph cohesion.

betweenness centrality
A graph metric used in NodeRAG to highlight nodes that act as bridges for information flow, identifying critical intermediaries.

Leiden algorithm
A community detection algorithm mentioned as an alternative to the label propagation algorithm, but not chosen for Zep's dynamic community extension due to its complexity.

K-means clustering
A clustering algorithm applied in NodeRAG to embeddings of semantic units, attributes, and high-level elements to identify semantically related nodes within communities.

semantic matching within community algorithm
An algorithm proposed in NodeRAG to establish meaningful connections between high-level element nodes and relevant nodes from the graph within the same community based on semantic similarity.

Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) algorithm
An approximate nearest neighbor search method used in NodeRAG to organize data into a multi-layer graph structure, enabling efficient retrieval of semantically similar nodes and integrated into the heterograph as semantic edges.

approximate nearest neighbor search
A class of algorithms that efficiently find points in a high-dimensional space that are approximately closest to a given query point.

cosine similarity
A measure of similarity between two non-zero vectors of an inner product space, often used in information retrieval to determine how similar two documents or vectors are.

dual search mechanism
A mechanism in NodeRAG that combines exact matching on title nodes and vector similarity search on rich information nodes to identify initial entry points in the heterograph.

Personalized PageRank (PPR) algorithm
A graph algorithm used in NodeRAG to identify relevant nodes by simulating a biased random walk starting from a set of entry points, refined for shallow execution.

shallow PPR
A variant of Personalized PageRank used in NodeRAG that limits the number of iterations to ensure relevance remains localized to the neighborhoods of entry points, preventing excessive diffusion.

cross nodes
Nodes identified by shallow PPR as closely related to entry points, included in the final retrieval results.

HotpotQA
A dataset used for evaluating token costs in the generation stage, likely focused on multi-hop question answering.

MuSiQue
A multi-hop question-answering dataset used to evaluate NodeRAG's performance, challenging models to combine information across multiple documents step-by-step.

RAG-QA Arena
An open-ended head-to-head evaluation framework used to assess the quality of retrieval-augmented generation systems on long-form question answering across six domains.

accuracy (Acc)
An evaluation metric measuring the correctness of answers generated by RAG methods.

average number of retrieved tokens (#Token)
An efficiency metric measuring the average quantity of tokens retrieved by RAG methods.

Score (Sco)
The original evaluation metric adopted for the MultiHop-RAG benchmark.

win and tie ratio (W+T)
An evaluation metric used in RAG-QA Arena to compare a system's generated answer against gold responses.

GPT 4o-mini
A large language model used to implement the RAG methods in the evaluation.

model temperature
A hyperparameter in LLMs that controls the randomness of output, influencing consistency and creativity.

ablation experiments
Experiments conducted to assess the impact of individual components of NodeRAG by systematically removing them.

top-k vector similarity method
A retrieval method that selects the 'k' most similar items based on vector embeddings, used as a comparison in ablation studies.

JPR
A RAG method that improves multi-answer retrieval by refining passage selection.

IR-CoT
A RAG method that integrates chain-of-thought reasoning for multi-hop question answering.

Tree of Clarifications
A RAG method that constructs a tree-based disambiguation structure to resolve ambiguous queries.

dense retrieval
A retrieval method that relies on vector embeddings to find similar documents.

context window limitations
A constraint in LLMs referring to the maximum amount of text they can process at once, impacting their ability to handle extensive external documents.

BioRAG
A RAG-LLM framework specifically designed for biological question reasoning.

MedicalRAG
A RAG method applied to medical LLM systems via graph retrieval-augmented generation.

corpus-wide understanding tasks
Tasks that require synthesizing knowledge across large datasets rather than just retrieving specific facts.

query-focused abstractive summarization
A task that involves generating a concise, high-level summary of information from a corpus, tailored to a specific query, which RAG sometimes struggles with.

Dense Hierarchical Retrieval (DHR)
A retrieval method that improves passage representations by combining macroscopic document semantics with microscopic passage details.

Hybrid Hierarchical Retrieval (HHR)
A retrieval method that fuses sparse and dense retrieval techniques for both document- and passage-level retrieval to achieve greater precision.

RAPTOR
A specific graph-based RAG method evaluated for its token costs in the generation stage across various datasets.

KAPING
A graph-based RAG method that refines knowledge organization and retrieval efficiency.

community-based summaries
Aggregated summaries generated for detected communities within a graph, used by methods like GraphRAG.

text embeddings
Numerical representations of text that capture semantic meaning, allowing for vector space comparisons.

top-k parameter
A hyperparameter used in retrieval methods to specify the number of most relevant items (e.g., text chunks, tokens) to retrieve.

LLM-as-a-Judge approach
An evaluation methodology where large language models are used to assess the quality of generated answers by other models.

Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG)
A framework that enhances Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning by integrating structured knowledge from external graphs. The paper proposes improvements to this framework.

Text-Attributed Graphs (TAGs)
A universal format for graph data used in GraphRAG, where nodes and edges possess textual attributes, unifying representation for various graph types including Knowledge Graphs.

Graph-Based Indexing (G-Indexing)
The initial phase of GraphRAG focused on constructing or identifying a graph database and establishing indices (graph, text, vector) to enhance the efficiency and speed of query operations.

Graph-Guided Retrieval (G-Retrieval)
The phase in GraphRAG that extracts pertinent information (nodes, triplets, paths, subgraphs) from the graph database in response to user queries, utilizing various retriever types and paradigms.

Graph-Enhanced Generation (G-Generation)
The final phase in GraphRAG where retrieved graph data is integrated with the query to synthesize meaningful outputs or responses, using generators like LLMs or GNNs and various graph formats.

Question Answering (QA)
A broad downstream task in NLP where GraphRAG is applied, encompassing sub-tasks like Knowledge Base Question Answering (KBQA) and Commonsense Question Answering (CSQA).

Knowledge Base Question Answering (KBQA)
A specific type of Question Answering where questions relate to and answers are derived from structured knowledge graphs, serving as a cornerstone application for GraphRAG systems.

Commonsense Question Answering (CSQA)
A specific type of Question Answering that involves using external commonsense knowledge graphs to reason and derive answers to multiple-choice questions requiring abstract commonsense knowledge.

BOCI PENG
An author of the survey 'Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey' affiliated with Peking University.

YUN ZHU
An author of the survey 'Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey' affiliated with Zhejiang University.

Ant Group
An organization that supported research in GraphRAG through its Ant Research Intern Program.

Peking University
A university affiliated with authors (Boci Peng, Yan Zhang) of the 'Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey' paper.

Wikidata
A collaboratively edited multilingual knowledge base, serving as a central storage for structured data and supported by LC-QuAD v2.

ConceptNet
A freely available semantic network designed to help computers understand the meanings of words people use.

WebQSP
A benchmark dataset for knowledge graph question answering, containing natural language questions that require reasoning over paths of up to two hops, used for evaluating model performance.

MetaQA
A movie domain dataset with over 400,000 questions structured around a knowledge graph, organized by reasoning hop difficulty.

BERT
A well-known text-encoder model used for generating embeddings for nodes or relationships.

RoBERTa
A robustly optimized BERT pretraining approach, used as a retriever model in some GraphRAG systems like Subgraph Retriever.

Transformer
The architectural foundation upon which many modern Large Language Models (LLMs) are built, enabling their advanced language processing capabilities.

Query Expansion
A technique within query enhancement that supplements or refines the original user query with additional relevant terms or concepts to improve retrieval results.

Knowledge Pruning
A technique within knowledge enhancement that involves filtering out less relevant or redundant retrieved information to refine the retrieval results and reduce noise.

Nodes (retrieval granularity)
A retrieval granularity in GraphRAG focused on extracting individual elements (entities or textual information) from the graph, suitable for targeted queries.

Subgraphs (retrieval granularity)
A retrieval granularity in GraphRAG that extracts interconnected sets of nodes and edges, offering comprehensive relational contexts and deeper insights.

Training-Free (training strategy)
A training strategy in GraphRAG where models (often closed-source LLMs or non-parametric retrievers) are used without explicit fine-tuning, relying instead on prompt engineering.

Joint Training
A training strategy in GraphRAG where retrievers and generators are trained simultaneously or in an alternating fashion to enhance their synergy and overall performance on downstream tasks.

Knowledge Graph (KG)
A type of graph constructed by extracting entities and relationships from each chunk.

E-commerce

Okapi BM25 full-text search
One of the three search functions implemented by Zep, used to identify relevant documents by measuring word similarities in full-text content, often relying on Neo4j's Lucene implementation.

Breadth-first search (BFS)
One of the three search functions implemented by Zep, used over knowledge graphs to enhance initial search results by identifying additional nodes and edges within n-hops, revealing contextual similarities.

Apache Lucene
An open-source search engine library whose implementation is utilized by Neo4j within Zep for features like cosine semantic similarity search and Okapi BM25 full-text search.

Multi-Session Chat dataset
A dataset introduced in 'Beyond Goldfish Memory: Long-Term Open-Domain Conversation', a 500-conversation subset of which is used in the Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) task.

BAAI
Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, the organization that developed the BGE-m3 models used by Zep for reranking and embedding tasks.

BGE-m3 models
Specific models developed by BAAI used by Zep for both reranking and embedding tasks in its experimental implementation due to their multi-lingual, multi-functionality, and multi-granularity capabilities.

gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18
A specific version of an OpenAI Large Language Model used by Zep for graph construction and for the chat agent generating responses in experiments.

gpt-4o-2024-11-20
A specific, more capable version of an OpenAI Large Language Model used by Zep for the chat agent generating responses in experiments, demonstrating improved performance with Zep.

gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09
A specific version of an OpenAI Large Language Model used for conducting the Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) evaluation to ensure direct comparability with MemGPT’s reported results.

AriGraph
A graph-based RAG system that uses distinct episodic and semantic subgraphs, an approach from which Zep's design draws inspiration.

Distill-SynthKG
A graph-based RAG system mentioned as a notable example of the limited application of breadth-first search in the RAG domain.

FinanceBench
A benchmark for financial question answering, mentioned as an example of established RAG benchmarks against which Zep's traditional RAG capabilities could be evaluated in future work.

BEIR
A heterogeneous benchmark for zero-shot evaluation of information retrieval models, mentioned as an example of established RAG benchmarks against which Zep's traditional RAG capabilities could be evaluated in future work.

Charles Packer
Lead author of the paper introducing MemGPT and the Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) task.

Di Wu
Lead author of the paper introducing the LongMemEval benchmark and dataset.

Episodic memory
A psychological model of human memory that represents distinct events, mirrored by Zep's Episode Subgraph.

Semantic memory
A psychological model of human memory that captures associations between concepts and their meanings, mirrored by Zep's Semantic Entity Subgraph.

Formal ontologies
Structured representations of knowledge domains, foundational in pre-LLM knowledge graph work, suggested as a promising area for further exploration within the Graphiti framework for LLM-generated KGs.
